source.title: Noisy Interpolation Learning with Shallow Univariate ReLU Networks
source.authors: Nirmit Joshi; Gal Vardi; N. Srebro

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes noisy interpolation in univariate regression, but it does not test any listed version: it does not compare random-label memorization with natural-label generalization, sweep network width, compare architectures or optimizers, vary batch size or dropout, measure sharpness, or remove memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The paper’s risk bounds and comparisons concern noisy regression interpolation with a minimum-weight-norm ReLU network or a linear-spline predictor. They do not establish the listed classification, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example results.
record.test_reason: The study proves risk bounds for noisy univariate regression with a minimum-weight-norm ReLU interpolator. It does not test any listed version: interpolation alone does not establish V1's natural-label versus random-label comparison, and unbounded width does not establish V2's effect of widening.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the catastrophic in-probability result is proved for a zero target with Gaussian noise; finite upper bounds require finite corresponding noise moments and Lipschitz targets. On equally spaced inputs, the authors state tempered behavior both in probability and in expectation. Their main conclusion concerns sensitivity to loss, sampling, and the distinction between expectation and high probability.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses minimum-weight-norm interpolation for a univariate two-layer ReLU regression network with an unregularized skip connection; it does not use the listed studies’ natural-label classification setups or standard gradient-training comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss exponent p, expectation versus in-probability risk, and random versus equally spaced input sampling change the reported behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: For random uniform inputs, minimum-norm ReLU interpolation has high-probability risk bounds proportional to noise risk divided by 2−p for 1 ≤ p < 2; Gaussian noise gives matching-order lower bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy univariate minimum-norm ReLU interpolation has tempered risk in probability for 1 ≤ p < 2, with deterioration as p approaches 2.

fits_no_version.finding: With random uniform inputs, a zero target and Gaussian noise, population and reconstruction risks diverge in probability for p ≥ 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-norm ReLU interpolation can exhibit catastrophic regression risk under random input sampling.

fits_no_version.finding: Equation (10) reports infinite expected population risk despite the high-probability bounds for p < 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tempered risk in probability need not imply finite expected risk over training sets.

fits_no_version.finding: Equally spaced training inputs yield tempered minimum-norm interpolation risk for every fixed p ≥ 1, assuming finite corresponding noise moments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-input spacing can change noisy interpolation from catastrophic to tempered.

fits_no_version.finding: The constant-extended linear spline has tempered risk for every fixed p ≥ 1 with finite corresponding noise moments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different interpolating predictors can have different risk behavior on the same noisy univariate regression problem.

record.problems: The analysis is limited to univariate regression with a specific minimum-weight-norm interpolator and noisy-label model; it does not measure classification accuracy, chance performance, or the listed version-specific interventions. The theorems are asymptotic, and no error bars or confidence intervals are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the auxiliary extended linear-spline variant ĥS: its infinite expected Lp risk and tempered-in-probability behavior are discussed in Section 3 and Appendix A, but it is an auxiliary construction rather than a listed-version result. No cited prior-work outcomes were extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Same-recipe natural-label and fixed-random-label fitting, held-out classification accuracy, and chance-level performance under random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The paper's challenge to tempered-overfitting predictions concerns a claim outside V1–V8; it does not challenge those versions.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels with training on natural labels; no natural-label held-out accuracy or chance-level random-label test accuracy.
No width sweep or test-error measurement across widths around the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No sharpness or other measured-property comparison against the training–test gap.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: minimum-norm unbounded-width univariate two-layer ReLU network f̂S
rows.operation_detail: Measures asymptotic population Lp risk under i.i.d. uniform inputs and noisy regression labels, in probability, for 1 ≤ p < 2.

conditions.value: y = f*(x) + ϵ; arbitrary non-zero noise distribution

rows.measure: Population Lp risk; Theorem 2 gives an upper bound and Theorem 3 a matching-order lower bound for f* ≡ 0 with Gaussian noise.
rows.value: Theorem 2: lim P[Lp(f̂S) ≤ C/(2−p) · Lp(f*)] = 1. Theorem 3: for f* ≡ 0 and Gaussian noise, lim P[Lp(f̂S) ≥ c/(2−p) · Lp(f*)] = 1.
rows.note: This is a noisy-regression population-risk result, not a test-error or accuracy result for any listed version.
rows.check: The bounds are theoretical results, not measured outcomes. Specify a Lipschitz target and finite noise p-th moment for a nontrivial finite upper bound. Lp(f*) is the noise risk, not zero when f* ≡ 0. Both theorems also bound reconstruction risk Rp.

rows.subject: minimum-norm unbounded-width univariate two-layer ReLU network f̂S
rows.operation_detail: Measures asymptotic population Lp risk under i.i.d. uniform inputs and Gaussian-noise regression labels, in probability, for p ≥ 2.

conditions.value: Gaussian, variance σ² for some constant σ > 0

rows.measure: Population reconstruction risk Rp and population Lp risk
rows.value: For any p ≥ 2 and b > 0, lim P[Rp(f̂S) > b] = 1 and lim P[Lp(f̂S) > b] = 1.
rows.note: The reported catastrophic regression risk is not a result on the listed versions’ test-error or accuracy measures.
rows.check: Correctly reports Theorem 4's divergence under a zero target and Gaussian noise. This is a theoretical regression result, with no width comparison or classification accuracy comparison.

rows.baseline: i.i.d. uniform input sampling in Sections 3–4; no numeric baseline stated
rows.value: Theorem 5: for any p ≥ 1, lim P[Rp(f̂S) ≤ Cp Lp(f*)] = 1 and lim P[Lp(f̂S) ≤ Cp Lp(f*)] = 1.

rows.subject: linear-spline interpolator ĝS
rows.operation_detail: Measures asymptotic population risk for noisy regression with i.i.d. uniform inputs.

conditions.value: y = f*(x) + ϵ; arbitrary non-zero noise distribution

rows.measure: Population reconstruction risk Rp and population Lp risk, in probability
rows.baseline: minimum-norm ReLU network result in Theorems 2–4; no numeric baseline stated
rows.value: Theorem 1: for any p ≥ 1, lim P[Rp(ĝS) ≤ Cp Lp(f*)] = 1 and lim P[Lp(ĝS) ≤ Cp Lp(f*)] = 1.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a linear-spline comparison, not a result for any listed version.
rows.check: Specify the Lipschitz target and finite noise p-th moment for a finite risk bound. The spline uses constant extensions outside the extreme training inputs; the alternative linear extensions have different expectation behavior. The result is theoretical.
